pr.title: Stop making any assumption about the projections applied to the upvars in the `ByMoveBody` pass
pr.description:
So it turns out that because of subtle optimizations like [`truncate_capture_for_optimization`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/ab5bda1aa70f707014e2e691e43bc37a8819252a/compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/upvar.rs#L2351), we simply cannot make any assumptions about the shape of the projections applied to the upvar locals in a coroutine body.

So stop doing that -- the code is resilient to such projections, so the assertion really existed only to "protect against the unknown".

r? oli-obk
Fixes #123650
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The historical defect is an ICE/debug assertion in `MakeByMoveBody`, not a runtime miscompilation. The old pass asserted that the projection remainder after remapping and optional deref-peeling was `[]` or `[Deref]`; with a truncated immutable capture it instead contained an extra field projection and the compiler panicked. The fix removes that assertion while keeping the same place constructed from `Field(remapped_idx, remapped_ty)`, then the bridging projections, then the final projections. Thus there is no historically incorrect *value-producing* transformation to encode: the original behavior is a compiler abort on the triggering shape, and the corrected behavior is a successful compile with unchanged runtime semantics. A function pair that both pass Miri and return different defined values cannot represent that difference without inventing an arbitrary semantic rewrite (for example replacing the assertion with a different result), which the task explicitly forbids. The regression test itself is `//@ check-pass` and only verifies that compilation no longer ICEs.

analysis.originalLogic: In `MakeByMoveBody`, when rewriting a place rooted at `ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL`, the pass matched the first field projection, looked up its remapping `(remapped_idx, remapped_ty, needs_deref, bridging_projections)`, optionally peeled one leading `Deref` when `needs_deref` was set, and then rebuilt the place as `Field(remapped_idx, remapped_ty)` followed by the bridging projections and the remaining `final_projections`. The pre-fix logic additionally asserted that `final_projections` could only be empty or a single `Deref`: "The only thing that should be left is a deref, if the parent captured an upvar by-ref." This assertion assumed the original coroutine upvar projection had a particular shape.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect assumption was the assertion `std::assert_matches::assert_matches!(final_deref, [] | [mir::ProjectionElem::Deref]);`. It treated the projection remainder after field remapping and optional deref-peeling as necessarily empty or exactly one `Deref`. Immutable captures can instead be truncated by `truncate_capture_for_optimization`, so the child upvar may project through fewer fields than expected (for example `&(*s)` instead of `&(*s.path)`), leaving additional field projections in the remainder. The correct fix is not a different rewrite of the place: it removes the shape assertion and continues chaining the bridging projections and final projections, renaming `additional_projections` to `bridging_projections` to document that they bridge from the old captured upvar to the parent coroutine-closure's upvar.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust coroutine-closure/async-closure source compiled with `#![feature(async_closure)]` (edition 2021) where a by-reference upvar is captured and a field is accessed through that reference inside an `async move ||` body. The triggering shape is an immutable parent reference such as `s: &Struct` with an access like `&s.path`, because truncation for optimization applies "ONLY when the upvar is immutable". Mutable-reference or otherwise untruncated captures may retain the fuller projection shape and not exercise the removed assertion. A contrasting program can use a mutable reference/capture so truncation does not collapse `&(*s.path)` to `&(*s)`; the two programs should differ only in the capture mutability/shape that controls truncation.
analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix for ICE #123650 in the coroutine `ByMoveBody` pass. The pass cannot assume the shape of projections applied to coroutine upvar locals: `upvar.rs`'s `truncate_capture_for_optimization` can shorten an immutable capture from `&(*s.path)` to `&(*s)`, so the projection remainder after remapping need not be empty or a single `Deref`. The fix removes the assertion and keeps applying bridging/final projections in order.
analysis.trigger: During generation of the by-move coroutine body, an upvar place begins with `CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL` plus a field, the field has a `field_remapping` entry, and the remaining projection after any required leading `Deref` is peeled contains something other than only `Deref` (notably a `Field` left by an immutable capture that was truncated). The old `assert_matches!(final_deref, [] | [mir::ProjectionElem::Deref])` then fails and produces an internal compiler error.
preconditions: The crate uses async closures/coroutine closures and the `ByMoveBody` transformation is being applied to a coroutine body (`#![feature(async_closure)]`, edition 2021 in the regression test).
An upvar is captured by reference and accessed inside the async move closure body, e.g. `let path = &s.path;` with `s: &Struct`.
The captured upvar is immutable, so `truncate_capture_for_optimization` may capture `&(*s)` instead of the longer `&(*s.path)` projection.
The projection rooted at the capture struct includes a field for which `field_remapping` supplies `remapped_idx`, `remapped_ty`, `needs_deref`, and bridging projections.
pitfalls: Do not assume that the only possible remainder after remapping and optional deref-peeling is `[]` or `[Deref]`; truncated immutable captures can leave field projections.
Truncation is conditional on immutability; testing only a mutable capture can miss the problematic projection shape.

Keep bridging projections from precise capturing and the final peeled-deref projections as separate ordered chains; the fix only renames/documentation-changes the bridging map and removes the assertion, preserving the place construction order.
This was an ICE/debug assertion, not a silent runtime miscompile; do not infer that removing the assertion changes the intended rewritten place semantics.
analysis.testStrategy: Add/run a UI `check-pass` regression test under `tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/` (the patch adds `truncated-fields-when-imm.rs`). Use `//@ edition: 2021`, `//@ check-pass`, `#![feature(async_closure)]`, a `pub struct Struct { pub path: String }`, and `pub fn test(s: &Struct) { let c = async move || { let path = &s.path; }; }`. The test comment documents that `truncate_capture_for_optimization` captures `&(*s)` only for immutable upvars, invalidating the `ByMoveBody` assumption. The compile must complete without the `ByMoveBody` assertion/ICE. To isolate the condition, contrast this immutable reference capture with a variant where truncation does not shorten the capture (e.g. mutable capture), keeping the rest of the source identical.
